# vortx.ai

> Encode on device. Decode with @emem. Don't move your files; deliver tokenised context. A satellite, telescope, rover, robot, drone or camera keeps its files; each observation, image or clip becomes one signed, content-addressed emem token; @emem decodes the token straight into any agent's context (ChatGPT, Claude, Agentforce, Dify, any MCP client), so agents know what is happening in the world, share one reference instead of drifting paraphrases, and check every byte. Every line below reads `verb noun ref key=value`. Numbers that change are not typed here; each has a live source under `count`.

## pages (one structure for people and agents; every section below mirrors one)
see       /                 the live Earth; @emem decodes one signed fact per visit: Cubbon Park, Bengaluru, NDVI
run       /#run             six devices, one published sample each, run end to end in the browser
encode    /#connect         your file, hashed on your device, nothing uploaded; tools/emem_point.py for the device
decode    /#decode          ask @emem; catch a drifted number; @emem in ChatGPT, Claude, Agentforce, Dify, VS Code
plug      /#plug            every way in, each asked live as the page loads: MCP tools/list, both A2A cards, REST with its ed25519 checked, the OpenAPI spec, the SDKs' newest releases
browse    /#samples         the ememdemo catalogue: Earth, Space, Machines; each note re-checked as it loads
open      /?s=<cid>         any sample, opened on the page (a globe pin, a card): it runs end to end, its picture drawn from bytes checked here
news      /press/           every release, upgrade and listing, dated; each date re-read live from the record that owns it; images and facts for press; as data: /data/timeline.json
plan      /#mission         the satellite plan, deliberately without a date
book      /#book            team time; the protocol is free
check     /proof/           every check, step by step: handoff, observers, token family, files, trust chain
read      /emem/ protocol · /geo-qa/ private tenancy · /eudr/ · /propcheck/ · /trust/ · /spatial-ai/ glossary · /research/ · /press/ newsroom

## run (the home page's workflows: each step is a request you can make yourself; rows 0-based)
satellite twlpco5kin6qlz5eplt2pjm7n4  Sentinel-2B scene, 351.0 MB  GET note → base32(blake3(note)[0:16])==cid → rebuild root → GET https://emem.dev/v1/tree/<cid>?row=68 (level 4 tile 0,0) → Range read 601,342 B from sentinel-cogs → blake3==row → inflate, undo predictor 2 → mean RGB 156,137,113 at 98% valid == the row's stats
telescope wkxa7tcmw2orf7ujjf5yi66dhe  Webb, Cosmic Cliffs, 143.7 MB  row 1 (strip 0 rows 0…4), 80.0 KB from esawebb.org
robot     qcoylkllqzfqnsinn4af5i2mi4  ALOHA arms, 502.5 MB MP4  row 3 (frames 5000…5001 · 100.0 s), 15.3 KB from huggingface.co (302 to its CDN)
drone     ejvovl6sz7d3sugfcrwwie4rma  OpenAerialMap survey  row 77 (level 6 tile 0,0), 13.2 KB; decode = the header row's JPEGTables + the tile
camera    t7ebh6s6imxrwdmizebnw52nwe  12 TfL cameras via geo.qa  row aldgate: GET clip → sha256 and blake3 == the row → GET https://emem.dev/v1/perception/verify/clip/<sha256> → ed25519 over the canonical payload JSON (sorted keys, no spaces), key yQOKkNB+c+zl9kxxanwcNTZLgtHBsLvQH+q8pECrm/Q= → NOAA sun from the signed lat, lng, captured_at within 0.1° of the note
machine   emem:trace:mxyer5c2oxn4ud3xqbtnaxcxhdv4kkxiu67q32inbwxgpa7r3s6a  POST /v1/trace_resolve → POST /v1/trace_verify (host.counters.v1 → admit) → chain, root and the device's ed25519, rechecked
send      Range           a single `Range: bytes=a-b` and no other header: esawebb.org, esahubble.org, oin-hotosm-temp and mux.dev refuse CORS preflights
fallback  range_hash      POST https://emem.dev/v1/range_hash {"url","offset","length"} when a source refuses browsers; signed, domain emem.range_hash.v1
count     moved           a token of 26 to 85 bytes instead of the file; each note costs ~1.2k to ~6.1k tokens to read, where the files cost ~91M to ~319M as raw bytes

## do
call      emem            https://emem.dev/mcp  transport=streamable-http  key=none  account=none
mention   @emem           ChatGPT app  https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a6a0832a59081918b19aec0ddf9ec77
add       emem            Claude Code  `claude mcp add --transport http emem https://emem.dev/mcp` · Claude: add https://emem.dev/mcp as a custom connector
connect   emem            Salesforce Agentforce, as a remote MCP server  url=https://emem.dev/mcp  key=none  how=https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/mcp-support/
install   emem            GitHub MCP Registry, one click for VS Code and Copilot  https://github.com/mcp/Vortx-AI/emem
configure emem            .vscode/mcp.json  {"servers":{"emem":{"type":"http","url":"https://emem.dev/mcp"}}}
list      emem            official MCP registry  io.github.Vortx-AI/emem
plug      emem            Dify marketplace, every tool, no key  https://marketplace.dify.ai/plugin/vortx-ai/emem
govern    emem            MuleSoft Anypoint Exchange, the Vortx AI MCP Server asset  https://anypoint.mulesoft.com/exchange/68e53915-e89b-4e82-b794-12d37982db4c/vortxAi-asset/
install   sdk             `pip install ememdev` · `npm i @vortxai/emem`
talk      a2a             card=https://emem.dev/.well-known/agent-card.json  run=POST https://emem.dev/a2a/tasks  async=POST https://emem.dev/v1/a2a/tasks
hand      a2a             this site's own card https://vortx.ai/.well-known/agent-card.json  protocol=A2A 1.0  tasks run on emem.dev
join      agora           https://emem.dev/a2a  inbox=POST https://emem.dev/v1/inbox {"to":"<your-pubkey8>"}
recall    facts           POST https://emem.dev/v1/recall {"place":"Cubbon Park, Bengaluru","bands":["indices.ndvi"]}  → cell defi.zb493.yiwo.zcb4e, NDVI 0.767258382642998 (Sentinel-2C, 16 Jun 2026)
ask       question        POST https://emem.dev/v1/ask {"q":"is this place flood-prone","place":"Ashok Nagar, Ranchi"}  fans out to twenty-plus signed readings under one receipt
gate      draft           POST https://emem.dev/v1/guard/verdict  deny=PROV_SIG|PROV_BYTES|PROV_DRIFT  fix=refresh_token|remove_reference|contact_admin|cite_observation
catch     drift           POST https://emem.dev/v1/guard/verdict {"texts":["… NDVI of 0.81 [emem:fact:defi.zb493.yiwo.zcb4e:eheadieomxr2zusgh4nx7mfisrtme23ztjiluyrfve64xoap6hka]"]}  → deny PROV_VALUE fix=correct_value
echo      number          POST https://emem.dev/v1/echo_verify {"token":"emem:fact:defi.zb493.yiwo.zcb4e:eheadieomxr2zusgh4nx7mfisrtme23ztjiluyrfve64xoap6hka","claimed_value":"0.767"}  → drift=rounded; "0.767258382642998" → matches; print values verbatim
point     file            https://vortx-ai.github.io/ememdemo/  leaves the bytes at the source, returns a signed pointer note

## encode (your file or device; https://vortx.ai/#connect writes the same note in the browser, byte for byte, nothing uploaded)
install   tools           `pip install blake3 "ememdev[signing]"`
encode    file            `python3 emem_point.py FILE [--source URL] [--stamp] > FILE.md`  https://vortx.ai/tools/emem_point.py  4 MiB ranges, blake3 per range, Merkle root, kind from the first bytes, laid out as the ememdemo pointers; --stamp adds after: sth <size> <root> <signed_at> once the log head verifies
name      note            cid26=base32(blake3(note)[0:16])  token=emem:tree:<cid26>#row=<i>  resolves once the note is published byte for byte
publish   note            `ememdev write --path /memories/by_attester/<you>/FILE.md --body-file FILE.md`  your own namespace, signed with your key (`ememdev whoami`)
decode    token           any agent with @emem reads the note, then fetches only the ranges it needs and checks each against its row
example   satellite       `python3 emem_point.py TCI.tif --source https://sentinel-cogs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/sentinel-s2-l2a-cogs/43/P/GQ/2026/5/S2B_43PGQ_20260512_0_L2A/TCI.tif --stamp > TCI.tif.md`
sign      at capture      hardware-held keys on the device: book an integration session (below)

## token
mint      emem:fact:<cell64>:<fact_cid>   len=83..85  fact_cid=base32(blake3(canonical CBOR)), 52 chars, never truncated
resolve   token                          POST https://emem.dev/v1/memory_token/resolve {"token":"emem:fact:…"}  returns fact + receipt; 409 if the cell and the bytes disagree
hash      fact                           GET https://emem.dev/v1/facts/<fact_cid>  accept=application/cbor  check=base32(blake3(body))==fact_cid
verify    receipt                        ed25519 over blake3("emem.preimage.v1\0" ‖ u32le(len) ‖ "receipt" ‖ tagged segments)  spec=https://emem.dev/v1/verifier_spec  js=https://emem.dev/emem-verify-core.js
verify    log head                       GET https://emem.dev/v1/log/sth  ed25519 over the emem.translog.sth.v1 preimage {1 tree_size u64be, 2 root, 3 signed_at, 4 responder_pubkey}
name      nine token shapes              fact (same bytes for everyone) · cell (an address, no body) · entity (a shared name, not shared bytes) · bundle · raster · cube · rasterset · trace · attestation
note      pointer.v1                     https://emem.dev/memories/by_attester/<pubkey8>/<cid26>.md  cid26=base32(blake3(note)[0:16])  (the catalogue header's "base32(blake3(bytes))[0:26]" means this: the first 16 bytes, encoded)
read      chunk                          GET <source> Range: bytes=<offset>-<offset+length-1>  check=base32(blake3(chunk))==row
root      pointer                        merkle over leaf=blake3(utf8(url) ‖ u64be(offset) ‖ u64be(length) ‖ hash32), pairs blake3(l‖r), odd node promoted; a `·` url is the empty string in the leaf
chain     feed                           link0=blake3(32 zero bytes ‖ hash0), linki=blake3(link(i-1) ‖ hashi), every row in order; GET /v1/tree does not apply
hash      range at source                POST https://emem.dev/v1/range_hash {"url","offset","length"}  signed, domain emem.range_hash.v1; for sources that refuse cross-origin reads

## samples (the ememdemo standard, kept on every page; https://vortx-ai.github.io/ememdemo/llms.txt is the catalogue)
line      catalogue       `verb kind cid key=value`: src size hashed=N/M at tok raw by t; tok=what reading the note costs, raw=the source's bytes as base64 (0.634 tokens per byte)
keep      by              machine (signed by a system) · third-party (a publisher's file) · combined (joined from several) · human (a person's file)
check     note            re-checked as each card loads: base32(blake3(note)[0:16])==cid → "✓ note", else "✗ name lies"; unreachable is not a failed check
show      picture         only the image a thumb.v1 note carries: its name matches, its of: is the record, its data:image line is the file shown; https://vortx.ai/data/thumbs.json maps record → thumb
print     values          verbatim, as signed; 0.767 for 0.767258382642998 is drift
open      sample          https://vortx.ai/?s=<cid>  by schema: pointer.v1 name, root, one row proved and read by range, then a whole overview level (every tile hashed) or the photo · world.v1 bundle signed and recomputed, every reading inside it, one echoed verbatim · grid.v1 each map's bundle, every square a member · timelapse.v1 three cubes signed, first and last frames' pixels hashed to their names · camera.v1 clip, geo.qa signature, sun · directory.v1 root, one file against its publisher hash

## family (one live example per shape; https://vortx.ai/proof/#tokens re-derives each in the browser)
fact      emem:fact:defi.zb493.yiwo.zcb4e:eheadieomxr2zusgh4nx7mfisrtme23ztjiluyrfve64xoap6hka  Cubbon Park NDVI 0.767258382642998  check=blake3(GET /v1/facts/<cid> as CBOR)==fact_cid; receipt names the cid
cell      emem:cell:defi.zb43b.mAga.yiwU  Europe's Spaceport, Kourou  GET /v1/cells/<cell64>/info  an address, no body until a fact hangs on it
entity    emem:entity:5pitnkcnle3cq6yldbffj52zja  GET /v1/entity/<cid>  derive=base32(blake3("emem.entity.v1|loc|"+cell64+"|"+kind+"|"+label)[0:16]), text normalised; an external anchor wins
bundle    emem:bundle:y2k6h2laeo4libfsiebucdw4mu  GET /v1/memory_bundle/<token>  derive=base32(blake3("emem.memory_bundle.v1|"+purpose+"\n"+per citation "cell|band|tslot|fact_cid\n")[0:16])
raster    emem:raster:23vfacx23nr3dwki6si4yrolmmp3wr6dtrhjxbw4rihiaafrpyga:s2.B08:20500:sw7lynliwyqfigyw6oqwso64wmulcumifqorfpfogkngjhsqzjpq  POST /v1/raster/resolve  check=blake3(GET /v1/artifacts/<artifact_cid>)==artifact_cid; each anchor == grid[row*w+col]; grid=EMEMGRD1, 64-byte header, f32le rows
cube      emem:cube:23vfacx23nr3dwki6si4yrolmmp3wr6dtrhjxbw4rihiaafrpyga:s2.B08:20500..20585:ganwwj25obuob3pp7pjtkd4awtihnluotdowe2cqtrj77af5qlna  POST /v1/cube/resolve  check=each slice as a raster
rasterset emem:rasterset:sml5syqegico2sobfkxjp2o2twwepdwve7753ubkoa5n27y22rba:zu5p3u4r5n5uinu2ghwzjo2272ztjvnnf7cnlt7hiqwxo4cq3hhq  POST /v1/raster_bundle/resolve  check=base32(blake3(canonical CBOR [member derivation cids…, "purpose:"+purpose]))
trace     emem:trace:mxyer5c2oxn4ud3xqbtnaxcxhdv4kkxiu67q32inbwxgpa7r3s6a  POST /v1/trace_resolve  check=segment chain (prev_digest), merkle v1 root (leaf 0x00, node 0x01, chain order), trace_cid, the DEVICE's ed25519 over the os_trace preimage; golden vector at /v1/verifier_spec
attest    emem:attestation:<cid>  POST /v1/trace_resolve  none backed by a manufacturer yet: vendor anchors are provisional, GET /v1/device_platforms
state     emem:state:6omzeryht75zyabeajuimcqzm7pzenvy3y6p4irwxdpt7x5ayimq  GET /v1/state/<cid>  check=blake3(canonical_cbor_hex)==cid; walk derived_from back through the answer's stages
tree      emem:tree:wkxa7tcmw2orf7ujjf5yi66dhe#row=1  Webb, Cosmic Cliffs  GET /v1/tree/<file_cid>?row=1  check=leaf from the note's row, log2(n) hashes to the note's root

## segment (who observes, and the emem profile that admits it; status live at https://emem.dev/v1/substrates)
observe   mars            space.deep.v1  subject anchored by identity, no latitude  pointer=fi67bt4rxkic3ssuag2v2hskly (Hubble's Mars)
observe   L2              space.deep.v1  Webb  pointer=wkxa7tcmw2orf7ujjf5yi66dhe
observe   moon            space.deep.v1  pointer=jxz6pghlsjbohvx6s5iw6yek4m (Kaguya terrain)
observe   hubble          observatory.telescope.v1  site is a cell, target an identity  pointer=7rn7fxbl75o5cijqpnok5oc7rq (M51)
capture   sentinel-2      earth.satellite.v0  the open archive, admitted by recomputation
sign      your satellites orbital.satellite.v1  at capture on the payload computer; trace includes power and thermal
lift      rockets         each object's launch is in its elements (international designator); a launch site is an emem:cell
fly       drones          aerial.drone.v1  pointer=ejvovl6sz7d3sugfcrwwie4rma
share     robots, rovers  robot.fleet.v1  pointer=lj4xi7iksjc4h3mr3prpz5gkne (ALOHA)
trace     any machine     host.counters.v1  scheduler, memory, storage, network
root      device keys     https://emem.dev/v1/device_platforms  hardware roots of trust by family

## ground (what https://vortx.ai/proof/#handoff runs in the browser, and the hero decodes once per visit; run it anywhere)
recall    indices.ndvi                   at a cell; pick the newest by sources[0].captured_at
mint      token                          emem:fact:<cell>:<fact_cid>; hand it to a second agent (the page uses a Web Worker)
hash      fact                           the second agent fetches the CBOR and recomputes the cid; values are read from those bytes only
verify    receipt                        with emem-verify-core (self-tested against the Rust signer's vectors)
parse     derivation.args                [lat, lng, scene, epsg, formula, [dn_B08, dn_B04], cloud_pct, used_max_cloud, used_lookback_d, scl, scenes_tried, (search_url), (dn_offset)]
project   lat,lng                        WGS84 → UTM(epsg), Snyder 1987 series, same as emem-fetch/src/proj.rs
locate    pixel                          col=round(i+(E−X)/sx) row=round(j+(Y−N)/sy) from ModelTiepoint and ModelPixelScale
read      tile                           one 1024×1024 tile per band, by HTTP Range, from sentinel-cogs on AWS Open Data
decode    tile                           DEFLATE, TIFF predictor 2, uint16
compute   ndvi                           r(dn)=(dn+offset)×1e-4; (r(B08)−r(B04))/(r(B08)+r(B04)) in f64 == the signed value, bit for bit
check     capture                        SGP4 on CelesTrak elements at captured_at; cell within 145 km cross-track (290 km swath), elements within 20 d of capture
count     bytes                          wire 83..85 B; the reader pulls about 3 MB of about 480 MB, from the source; zero bytes of imagery pass between agents

deploy    geo.qa          https://geo.qa  your cameras, drones, satellites and sensors; only your agents read it; boundary enforced per organisation in code
prove     eudr.dev        https://vortx.ai/eudr/  in testing: forest loss after 31 Dec 2020 on a plot, with a receipt an auditor re-checks
check     propcheck.dev   https://vortx.ai/propcheck/  in testing: flood, heat and land-change history of an address

## verify this site
hash      files           https://vortx.ai/.well-known/site-manifest.json  blake3 of every served file; release cid = base32(blake3(canonical core))
run       check           `python3 tools/site_manifest.py --verify`
list      claims          https://vortx.ai/.well-known/facts.json  every number the site asserts, with the source that can refute it
register  release         each release as a signed emem record under /memories/by_attester/<pubkey8>/vortx.ai/releases/ (live once the signing key is set; the manifest verifies offline either way)
